title: Preparation of screening assays for ADP-ribosyl readers and erasers using the GAP-tag as a binding probe
protocol: Prepare the mono-ADP-ribosylation reaction mix.
Let the reaction incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 h.
Add again 15 μL of PtxS1 and 15 μL of NAD+ to the reaction mixture.
Let the reaction incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 h.
Prepare a 5 mL HiTrap IMAC HP column by charging it with NiSO4 and equilibrate it with lysis buffer.
Load the reaction mixture to the column at 1 mL/min.
Wash the column with 5 column volumes of lysis buffer.
Elute the ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP using elution buffer.
Exchange the buffer to SEC buffer using a 15 mL Amicon centrifugal filter with 10 kDa molecular weight cutoff.
Concentrate the IMAC eluate to approximately 0.5–1 mL using a centrifugal filter.
Aliquot the protein into PCR reaction tubes (5–25 μL per tube).
Flash freeze the aliquoted tubes in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen aliquots at −70°C or below.
Optionally, analyze the modification of the protein by mass spectrometry to detect an additional monoisotopic mass of 541.061 Da for mono-ADP-ribosylation.
If required for binders of poly-ADP-ribose, use the mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP immediately or store it overnight (up to 24 h) at 4°C for further modification by PARP2.
Prepare the poly-ADP-ribosylation reaction mix for YFP-GAP in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Avoid mixing high concentrations of NAD+ and PARP2 during preparation of the mixture.
Mix all components and add PARP2 last.
Immediately gently mix by inverting the tube.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Let the reaction incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 2 h.
Remove unreacted NAD+, side-products and PARP2 by IMAC.
Prepare a 5 mL HiTrap IMAC HP column by charging it with NiSO4 and equilibrate it with lysis buffer.
Load the reaction mixture to the column at 1 mL/min.
Wash the column with 5 column volumes (CV) of lysis buffer.
Elute the poly-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP using elution buffer.
Exchange the buffer to SEC buffer using a 15 mL Amicon centrifugal filter with 10 kDa molecular weight cutoff.
Concentrate the IMAC eluate to approximately 0.5–1 mL using the same centrifugal filter.
Aliquot the protein in PCR reaction tubes (5–25 μL per tube).
Flash freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen.
Store the aliquots at -70°C or below.
Aliquot the protein into PCR reaction tubes (5–25 μL per tube).
Flash freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen.
Store the aliquots at −70°C or below.
Use black polypropylene plates for the FRET assay.
Prepare in assay buffer 50 μL of FRET assay mixture containing 1 μM CFP-fusion protein and 5 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP.
Prepare in assay buffer 50 μL of control mixture 1 containing 1 μM CFP-fusion protein and 5 μM unmodified YFP-GAP.
Prepare in assay buffer 50 μL of control mixture 2 containing 1 μM CFP-fusion protein, 5 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP and 200 μM ADP-ribose.
Optional: Prepare in assay buffer 50 μL DMSO test mixture containing 1 μM CFP-fusion protein, 5 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP and 1% (v/v) DMSO.
Pipette four times 10 μL of assay buffer into separate wells of a black 384-well plate.
Pipette each mixture prepared in the previous steps into separate wells of a black 384-well plate.
Incubate the plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 min.
Measure the fluorescence emission of each well using a multimode plate reader.
Set up a protocol for two separate fluorescence intensity measurements per well.
Excite samples with an excitation wavelength of 430 nm and measure emission at 477 nm.
Set the excitation wavelength to 430 nm with a bandwidth of 20 nm.
Set the emission wavelength to 527 nm with a bandwidth of 10 nm.
Keep all other settings identical to those used in the previous step.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of buffer-only wells as blanks.
Subtract the average blank fluorescence from each sample well's fluorescence intensity for both wavelengths.
Calculate the ratiometric FRET signal by dividing the fluorescence intensity at 527 nm by that at 477 nm.
Evaluate the rFRET signal for samples containing the FRET assay mixture.
Compare the rFRET signal to control mixtures 1 and 2.
If 200 μM ADP-ribose inhibits the signal less than expected, refer to troubleshooting guidelines.
Ensure DMSO test control does not have an rFRET value significantly lower than the FRET assay mixture.
Consider a difference of 0.2–0.3 in the FRET ratio as sufficient for setting up a screening assay.
If the difference in rFRET is larger (e.g., 1.0–1.5), use a lower protein concentration.
Refer to the NCBI online resource “Assay Guidance Manual” for more extensive validation instructions.
Prepare a dose-response curve with a serial dilution series of ADP-ribose optionally.
Prepare in assay buffer 250 μL of 2× FRET assay mixture containing 2 μM CFP-fusion protein and 10 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP.
Prepare a 2× concentrated half-logarithmic serial dilution starting at a concentration of 2 mM ADP-ribose in assay buffer.
Pipette four times 5 μL for each concentration of the 2× concentrated dilution series into columns 3–12 of a 384-well assay plate.
Pipette four times 5 μL buffer into column 2 of the assay plate.
Pipette four times 10 μL buffer into column 1 of the assay plate.
Dispense 5 μL of the 2× FRET assay mixture into each well in columns 2–12.
Spin down the plate at 500–1000×g for 5 min to remove potential air bubbles if an automated dispenser has been used.
Let the plate incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 min after preparation or dispensing steps.
Cover the plate with a lid or adhesive seal during incubation and between steps to prevent evaporation and dust accumulation.
Transfer compounds dissolved in DMSO to a screening plate using Echo 650.
Transfer 20 nL of the 10 mM compound stocks to a 384-well assay plate.
Dispense the compounds to wells in columns 4–24 according to a specified layout.
Optional: Add 20 nL of DMSO to control wells.
Cover the plate with a lid if used on the same day for screening.
Seal the plate with an adhesive seal if stored for a longer period.
Store the plate at −20°C until use if sealed with an adhesive seal.
Prepare solutions required for the screening.
Test rFRET signal on a small scale before starting the screening to ensure comparability.
If significantly lower signals are observed, prepare recombinant proteins freshly.
Prepare 4 mL of FRET assay mixture containing 1 μM CFP-fusion protein and 5 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP.
Prepare 200 μL of the ADP-ribose control mixture containing 1 μM CFP-fusion protein, 5 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP, and 200 μM ADP-ribose.
Dispense solutions using a Formulatrix Mantis low-volume liquid dispenser (10 μL/well) according to the layout in Figure 3.
Transfer buffer to column 1.
Transfer FRET assay solution to columns 2 and 4–24.
Transfer ADP-ribose control solution to column 3.
Spin down the plate at 500–1000×g for 5 min to remove potential air bubbles.
Determine the rFRET signal of each well as shown in step 6f.
Calculate the apparent inhibition percentages for each well containing screening compounds.
Set the average rFRET value of the control FRET assay mixture (column 2) to 0% inhibition.
Set the average rFRET value for the ADP-ribose control mixture (column 3) to 100% inhibition.
Prepare in assay buffer 90 μL of 2× FRET assay mixture containing 2 μM CFP-fusion protein and 10 μM mono-ADP-ribosylated YFP-GAP.
Prepare 25 μL of 400 μM ADP-ribose in assay buffer.
Prepare a 2× concentrated half-logarithmic serial dilution starting at a concentration of 200 μM compound, with each step diluted by 1:3.16.
Transfer four times 5 μL for each concentration of the prepared 2× concentrated compound dilution series into a 384-well assay plate (columns 3–8).
Transfer 5 μL of 400 μM ADP-ribose to each well in column 2.
Dispense 5 μL of the 2× FRET assay mixture into each well in rows A and B.
Fill each well to a final volume of 10 μL using assay buffer.
Spin down the plate at 500–1000×g for 5 minutes.
Determine the rFRET signals as shown in step 6f.
Use the respective wells containing the compound in buffer as a blank.
Subtract the average fluorescence intensities of wells C8 and D8 from those of wells A8 and B8.
Calculate the apparent inhibition percentages as described in step 13.
Perform dose-response curve analysis to determine IC50 values for each compound.

Validate compounds showing desired inhibition through further testing methods such as functional assays, isothermal titration calorimetry, surface plasmon resonance, differential scanning fluorimetry or protein X-ray crystallography.
Establish the assay with other ADP-ribosyl binding or hydrolyzing proteins to test specificity of the inhibitor.
